speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound shows normal kidneys, which makes a kidney stone less likely. Since you still have right flank pain and hematuria, is the pain sharp or dull, and has it radiated to your groin? Have you noticed any burning sensation when urinating or changes in the frequency of urination?

REQUEST TEST: CT KUB (Kidneys, Ureters, Bladder).

speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: Lower Urinary Tract Irritation / Early Urothelial Carcinoma.

Given the normal renal ultrasound and CT KUB, kidney stones and large masses are effectively ruled out. The combination of persistent hematuria and flank pain suggests pathology within the bladder or urethra that was missed on the initial scans. Can you confirm if you have a history of smoking, industrial chemical exposure, or any prior urinary tract infections?
